title: docket task catalog
description: The document `docket schema` emits: a machine-readable description of every task type docket registers. Unlike the other schemas in this directory, which each describe one line of a JSON-lines stream, this describes one whole document - validate it as a unit. See docs/task-catalog.md.

version.description: The catalog wire format. Independent of the --json event stream's version; branch on it so a future schema change does not silently break a consumer.

tasks.description: The task types the document describes, sorted by `type`. Every registered task type unless `docket schema --task` narrowed it.

type.description: The registry key - the name a recipe uses to invoke the task, such as `dokku_apps_property`.

synopsis.description: One-line description of what the task manages.

deprecation.description: The deprecation notice. Present only on a deprecated task; it names the replacement.

requirements.description: Plugin prose, one line per non-core plugin the task needs, in declared order. Absent when it needs nothing beyond dokku core. The Dokku floor is minimum_dokku_version; this array stays plugin prose only.

minimum_dokku_version.description: Oldest Dokku release this task's probe parses, as major.minor.patch. Absent when the task declares no floor. plan, apply, and export refuse the task when the server is older, unless --ignore-version is set.

plugin_requirements.description: Non-core plugins the task needs. name is the plugin:list name when it is fixed. name_field is the recipe key whose value is that name. when is the recipe key that must be true before the requirement applies. An installed plugin older than minimum is refused the same way an old Dokku is; a plugin that is not installed is left to the task's own probe.

export.description: Whether `docket export` can reconstruct the task from a live server.

probe.description: How much of its own state the task can read back. `unsupported` means it reports drift on every run and never converges.

fields.description: The recipe keys the task accepts, in declaration order.

property_schema.description: Present only for a task that manages an enumerable dokku property table. Its absence on a task that has a `property` field means the legal names are not enumerable from docket, not that there are none.

examples.description: The task's documented examples, the same ones its reference page publishes.

name.description: The plugin:list name, such as letsencrypt. Absent when name_field names the recipe key that carries it.

minimum.description: Oldest plugin release this task's probe parses, as major.minor.patch.

when.description: Recipe key that must be true before this requirement applies, such as global on dokku_certs.

name_field.description: Recipe key whose value is the plugin:list name, such as service on a datastore task.

caveat.description: Human-readable note explaining anything short of supported.

keys.description: The recipe keys that decide which resource the task manages, in the order a resource address renders them. A key holding its zero value is omitted from the address. Equal to the fields carrying `"identity": "key"`, in declaration order.

collections.description: The collection fields the task manages wholesale.

item.description: What identifies one entry: the element value, the map key, or the element struct's own identity keys.

item_keys.description: The element's own identity key names. Present only when `item` is `fields`.

type.description: The doc-facing type. A named string type such as a state enum is `string`; an optional pointer field is its element type.

required.description: Whether a recipe must supply the field. A field carrying a `default` is never required, because the default is filled in before the missing-field check runs.

default.description: The literal default, to be read according to `type`. On a pointer field it documents what the task coerces an omitted key to, not a value written into the recipe.

choices.description: The permitted values. Absent when the field is not an enum.

sensitive.description: The value is a secret. A consumer that echoes a recipe must mask it.

runner_file.description: The value names a file docket reads on the machine it runs on rather than on the dokku server, so the file must exist there even over `--host`. Absent on a field that is not one.

write_only.description: The server stores the value but never returns it, so an exported task leaves the field empty or lifts it into a required input with no value. A consumer refreshing state keeps the configured value rather than reporting drift. A probe may still verify the value by comparison. Absent on a field that is read back.

apply_only.description: The value steers how apply runs and is not server state, so an exported task carries its zero value or default. A consumer refreshing state keeps the configured value rather than reporting drift. Absent on a field that is server state.

identity.description: `key` selects which resource the task manages; `collection` is a set of items the task manages wholesale. Absent on a field that is neither.

item.description: The element shape of a list or dict. Absent on a scalar.

key_type.description: The map key's type. Present only on a dict.

type.description: The element's type. `object` means the element is a structured entry whose shape is spelled out in `fields`; `any` means the element is untyped.

identity.description: What identifies one entry. Present only on a field tagged as a collection - an untagged list is an attribute of the resource rather than the set of items the task manages.

keys.description: The element's own identity key names. Present only when `identity` is `fields`.

fields.description: The element's own fields, in declaration order. Present only when `type` is `object`. An element declares the same tags a task does, which is where a consumer learns that a nested value is a secret.

subcommand.description: The dokku subcommand a set or unset runs, e.g. `apps:set`.

field.description: The recipe key this table constrains.

dynamic.description: Name families the table cannot enumerate, because dokku validates them through the set subcommand rather than through its report schema. A name matching one of these prefixes is legal even though it is absent from `properties`.

rejected.description: Name families this task refuses because another task manages them. A name matching one of these prefixes is absent from `properties` for a different reason than a typo is, and reporting it as an unknown name sends the user looking through a list it will never be in.

name.description: The value a recipe puts in `property:`.

scopes.description: Where the property may be used. Using it in a scope it does not list is rejected at validate time, matching dokku's own rejection.

app_report_key.description: The key `dokku <plugin>:report --format json` emits for the property per app. Absent when the property has no per-app form.

global_report_key.description: The key `dokku <plugin>:report --global --format json` emits for the property. Absent when the property has no global form.

prefix.description: What a member's name starts with.

probeable.description: Whether the plugin's report surfaces a row per set member, so docket can read the value back. `false` means a recipe using the family reports drift on every run and never converges.

scopes.description: Where a member of the family may be used. Using one in a scope it does not list is rejected at validate time, matching dokku's own rejection.

sensitive.description: Members' values are treated as secrets.

prefix.description: What a member's name starts with.

replacement.description: The task type to write the property against instead. Always a `type` present elsewhere in this catalog.

reason.description: Why this task does not manage the family, phrased as a clause that reads after a semicolon.

name.description: The heading the reference page gives the example.

yaml.description: The YAML snippet, ready to paste into a recipe's task list.
